title: Margot Robbie Teams Up with “The Drama” Director for Upcoming Film, Deadline Reports
body:
Margot Robbie’s next cinematic venture has been confirmed: the Oscar‑winning actress will headline the upcoming A24 and Square Peg production “The Week of Pain,” directed by Kristopher Borgli, the filmmaker behind the critically lauded thriller “The Drama.” The casting news arrives as Robbie wraps filming on the highly anticipated “Ocean’s” prequel, signaling that the Australian star is already lining up new material rather than taking a hiatus.

“The Week of Pain” marks a notable shift for both Robbie and Borgli. Known for her chameleon‑like ability to inhabit vastly different roles—from the manic energy of “Birds of Prey” to the period elegance of “Barbie”—Robbie is now set to tackle a darker, more psychological narrative under the banner of A24, a studio synonymous with bold, auteur‑driven projects. Borgli, who earned praise for his unsettling storytelling in “The Drama,” is expected to bring his signature blend of tension and emotional nuance to the new film, which, according to insiders, explores themes of grief, trauma, and the thin line between victim and perpetrator.

Industry analysts view the partnership as a strategic alignment of talent and brand. A24’s recent slate has included genre‑bending titles such as “Everything Everywhere All at Once” and “The Green Knight,” both of which have bolstered the company’s reputation for nurturing distinctive voices. By attaching Robbie—one of the most bankable names in contemporary Hollywood—to a project that leans into the indie‑art house aesthetic, A24 aims to broaden its appeal to mainstream audiences without sacrificing its curatorial edge. For Robbie, the collaboration offers an opportunity to further diversify her résumé, reinforcing her reputation as an actress unafraid to oscillate between blockbuster franchises and risk‑taking cinema.

The production is being co‑produced by Square Peg, the Los Angeles‑based company founded by former Disney executives, which has been quietly building a portfolio of prestige pictures. Their involvement suggests a modest budget paired with high production values, a formula that has proven successful for similar A24 co‑productions. While specific plot details remain under wraps, early reports indicate that “The Week of Pain” will follow a woman confronting a series of harrowing events over a single, tumultuous week—an intense character study that will likely demand Robbie’s full emotional range.

Robbie’s decision to sign on while still finalizing work on the “Ocean’s” prequel underscores a broader trend among A‑list talent to maintain a steady pipeline of projects, mitigating the risk of prolonged gaps between releases. In a market where streaming platforms and theatrical windows are constantly evolving, staying visible across multiple mediums can preserve an actor’s relevance and bargaining power. Moreover, the actress’s involvement in an A24 film may position her favorably for future awards consideration, given the studio’s track record of producing Oscar contenders.

As production gears up for “The Week of Pain,” anticipation is already building among both fans and critics. The combination of Robbie’s star power, Borgli’s unsettling directorial style, and A24’s reputation for daring storytelling promises a film that could resonate on both commercial and artistic levels. If the project lives up to the early buzz, it may not only add another compelling entry to Robbie’s filmography but also further cement A24’s status as the go‑to home for high‑concept, character‑driven cinema. The industry will be watching closely as filming commences later this year, with a likely release slated for the 2025 awards season.
